newsitem.title: USA: Second fugitive surrenders after nationwide manhunt.
newsitem.headline: Second fugitive surrenders after nationwide manhunt.

text.p: A fugitive wanted on attempted murder charges surrendered in Utah Tuesday, one day after his brother turned himself in to authorities saying he had feared for his life, officials said.
Chevie Kehoe, 24, was arrested in Cedar City, Utah, according to the FBI. He was being taken to Salt Lake City to appear before a U.S. magistrate.

Kehoe and his brother, Cheyne, 21, were the subjects of a nationwide manhunt after a shootout with police in Ohio was recorded by police video cameras and aired on television. They were stopped for driving with expired license plates.
The brothers face a 16 count indictment in Ohio, including charges of attempted murder.

Chevie was believed to have been working on a small ranch in southwest Utah for some time. Both he and his younger brother have been regarded by law enforcement officials as armed and extremely dangerous.

Police said Cheyne Kehoe used a church pastor as an intermediary and turned himself in at the county courthouse at Colville, Washington, Monday. He declined to answer reporters' questions when he surrendered, but in a statement he read before he was taken inside, he said he chose to turn himself in because he feared for his safety.

"The reason I acted in the manner I did was due to the actions taken against men like Randy Weaver, Gordon Kahl and Bob Mathews," he said. "When the government law enforcement agencies abused the individual rights of these men, I feared for my life."
Weaver, a white separatist, was involved in an FBI standoff in 1992 at his remote cabin in Ruby Ridge, Idaho. His son and wife were killed along with a federal marshal.
Kahl, a militant tax protester, got into a gun battle that killed two U.S. marshals in North Dakota in 1983. He was killed later that year in a shootout with police in Arkansas.
Mathews died in a 1984 fire that followed an exchange of gunfire with the FBI on Whidbey Island, Washington.
